articles.title_orig: The ‘Musk selloff’ deepens as Tesla and SpaceX combine for $450 billion two-day wipeout
articles.title_zh: The ‘Musk selloff’ deepens as Tesla and SpaceX combine for $450 billion two-day wipeout
articles.content_orig:
The two companies helmed by the world's richest person have had a rough two-day stretch on the market. Tesla ( TSLA -10.77% ) closed at $398.50 on Election Day, and by 3:08 p.m. ET Thursday, it was trading at about $342, down 14%, representing a loss of about $225 billion in market value. SpaceX ( SPCX -9.05% ) fell from $141.31 to about $125, down 12%, or about $227 billion. Together, that's about $450 billion gone in two sessions, most of it on Thursday, when Tesla fell about 11% and SpaceX about 8%.
To illustrate how steep the drop has been, SpaceX is now trading below its $135 IPO price from June.
Image source: Getty Images.
If you had to sum it up in one word: politics. Democrats now control both chambers of Congress, and Musk, a top ally of President Donald Trump, is a likely target. Speaking on the All-In podcast on election night, Texas Republican Sen. Ted Cruz said Democrats had signaled they would use subpoenas "to go after Elon Musk." In Texas, home to both companies, voters elected a Democratic attorney general for the first time since 1994.
But political sentiment isn't the only reason. The Nasdaq was headed for its worst day in 18 months on Thursday as investors dumped chip and data-center stocks, on fears that new leaders in Washington and the states could slow data-center construction. SpaceX, of course, is exposed: Last month, it committed to a roughly $40 billion lease for AI chips with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, with payments starting in the first half of 2027.
Adding to the fire for SpaceX, Wall Street is reportedly trying to sell off pieces of that $40 billion chip deal to other investors, with Goldman Sachs and Apollo leading the effort, according to Bloomberg on Thursday.
SpaceX made money last quarter: $2.79 billion in operating income and $4.4 billion in net income, though it's still $413 million in the red for the first nine months of the year. Nothing that happened in Washington this week changes its launch business or Starlink.
But the fine print, or at least the filing details, are worth noting. That net income included a $390 million tax benefit and a $561 million unrealized gain on its stake in the Boring Company, Musk's tunneling firm, and two customers made up about half of quarterly revenue. Even after the drop, SpaceX is valued at about $1.7 trillion, roughly 150 times its third-quarter operating income on an annualized basis.
Part of Tesla's bull case rests on robotaxis. On Tesla's October earnings call , CFO Vaibhav Taneja told analysts he expects robotaxis to make a real dent in both sales and profits in 2027, and the firm said the Cybercab was due to launch in Dallas this month. Musk told analysts Tesla will end up doing "a majority of all passenger miles on earth" -- "unless we are stopped by governments."
That caveat matters more this week. Self-driving cars depend on regulators, and Washington just got less friendly to Musk. Taneja also conceded that the robotaxi business hasn't yet reached its cost target of 30 cents per mile.
The two companies are also tied together. Tesla's filing puts its SpaceX stake at $2.87 billion as of Sept. 30, and shows SpaceX with a $729 million balance owed to Tesla, most of it tied to Megapack batteries still on order. Bad news for one tends to hit the other.
Not all at once. The political risk is real, but for now it's mostly talk. The new Congress isn't seated until January, and investigations take time. Meanwhile, a two-day drop of 12% to 14% doesn't make either stock cheap.
If you believe in Musk's long-term plans, this is a reasonable time to start a position slowly. Buy in small pieces over several weeks, and keep it a small part of your portfolio, because these are among the most volatile tech stocks you can own.
If you can only pick one, SpaceX gives you a launch and satellite business that's already earning money, while much of Tesla's value rides on robotaxis that are just getting started. And if headlines out of Washington would keep you up at night, it's fine to wait until the political picture is clearer.

articles.title_orig: Oil prices hit two-month low following decisive midterm election results
articles.title_zh: Oil prices hit two-month low following decisive midterm election results
articles.content_orig:
Crude oil prices jumped Thursday, as investors reassessed the outlook for ‌the US-Israeli war with Iran while new attacks on tankers fed worries about oil supplies.
Brent crude futures rose 4% to $98.44 a barrel by 2:42 p.m. ET. US West Texas Intermediate crude increased 2.9% to $90.71 a barrel.
On Wednesday, both benchmarks tumbled more than 8% to their lowest settlement levels since August 31.
"The situation in the Middle East is ​still unresolved and that's why there is some modest recovery in prices at the moment," said Giovanni Staunovo, commodity analyst at UBS.
Andy Lipow, ​president of Lipow Oil Associates, said reports of tankers striking mines in the Middle East or being targeted by drones continue ⁠to worry the oil market. Investors are also worried about Iran's unchanged position regarding negotiations with the US.
Attacks on tankers in the Gulf are ​still running close to a record pace with at least five vessels having reported incidents since Sunday, according to UK maritime security agency UKMTO. The pace was ​similar to October when the agency said 35 vessels were hit, the most of any month of the war.
The war on Iran, which US President Donald Trump launched along with Israel in February, resulted in sharply higher fuel prices, which became major grievances for voters. Democrats took control of both houses of the US Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, routing Trump's ​Republican Party.
The new Democratic-controlled Congress takes office in January.
Citi said in a note there were concerns that with the midterms over, the White House could ​focus on its executive powers in foreign policy and potentially escalate the war with Iran.
Eurasia Group, however, lowered its estimate for the chance of renewed US strikes on ‌Iran ⁠to 60% from 65%. It also cut the probability of a deal to 10% from 20%, as Iran has held firm on demands that Trump is viewed as unlikely to accept. Eurasia Group raised the likelihood of a continued standoff to 30% from 15%.
Despite the recent drop in oil prices, any escalation in the conflict could push Brent into a $110 to $125 per barrel range, Eurasia Group said in a note.
Meanwhile, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi discussed the "latest progress" in diplomatic efforts to ​promote regional stability in separate calls ​with his Saudi and Qatari counterparts, the ⁠Iranian foreign ministry said.
Tensions in the region remain elevated. Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil exporter, issued alerts on Thursday warning of potential danger in Yanbu, the kingdom's Red Sea oil export hub, as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis continued attacks on the kingdom ​in another front of the Iran war.
The Houthis later said they attacked King Fahd airport in the Saudi city of Dammam, although ​there was no immediate ⁠confirmation from Saudi authorities.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents after attempting to use unauthorised routes through the Strait of Hormuz.
Elsewhere, Ukraine renewed attacks on Russian oil refineries, raising concerns about Russia's ability to export diesel under a deal with Trump.
The Ryazan oil refinery, one of Russia's largest, ⁠appeared to ​have been targeted in a large overnight drone attack on industrial sites southeast of Moscow, ​according to a Reuters video analysis.
If confirmed, it would be the second Russian refinery hit this week, following an attack on the Yaroslavl plant on Monday night.

articles.title_orig: Avigdor Liberman drops veto on haredi parties in coalition, opposition in talks with UTJ
articles.title_zh: Avigdor Liberman drops veto on haredi parties in coalition, opposition in talks with UTJ
articles.content_orig:
Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman has dropped his veto on forming a government with haredi (ultra-Orthodox) parties, opening the door for the opposition bloc to begin discussions with United Torah Judaism (UTJ), N12's Amit Segal reported on Thursday
The bloc is reportedly discussing the possibility of drafting a more lenient military conscription law, and the current assumption is that Shas would be forced to support the move as well, under pressure from Rabbi Lando.
UTJ , a longtime coalition partner of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , declined to recommend a candidate for prime minister to President Isaac Herzog during the party's consultation earlier on Thursday.
UTJ's decision to abstain came amid reported tensions between the haredi party and Netanyahu, and it benefits the opposition bloc seeking to replace him. Opposition party leaders have recently signaled greater openness to including haredi parties in their coalition.
A potential coalition led by Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot and including United Torah Judaism (UTJ) would hold 55 seats in the Knesset, falling short of the 61-seat majority needed to form a government. However, it would reduce Netanyahu's bloc to just 46 seats, potentially allowing Eisenkot to form a minority government with Ra'am and the Joint List abstaining.
Yisrael Beytenu denied the report in a statement to The Jerusalem Post .
"We are not aware of any such thing. Nothing has changed since the briefing was given," the party stated.
During the Monday briefing, Liberman ruled out joining a unity government with Netanayhu, along with the option of a minority government that would be reliant on support from the Arab parties. However, his stance regarding joining a coalition with  Shas and UTJ appeared to be more lenient.
Liberman stated that whoever would accept his set of principles and a conscription law to draft the haredim, he would "have no problem with."
Liberman has repeatedly ruled out joining a government with haredi parties in recent years, citing fundamental disagreements over military conscription and issues related to religion and state. He has previously declared that Yisrael Beytenu would not sit with either Arab or haredi parties, describing them as "non-Zionist elements" and arguing that anyone who refuses military service should be considered an evader.
His opposition to compromising on haredi conscription has also shaped coalition negotiations, most notably in 2019, when his refusal to support a compromise on a military draft law helped derail Netanyahu's efforts to form a government, triggering a political deadlock that led to five elections being held between 2019 and 2022.

articles.title_orig: China and the Netherlands Discuss Plant Breeders’ Rights, AI and Robotics
articles.title_zh: China and the Netherlands Discuss Plant Breeders’ Rights, AI and Robotics
articles.content_orig:
Protecting new plant varieties and applying artificial intelligence and robotics were central to discussions between Chinese and Dutch industry representatives at the 24th China Kunming International Flower Expo.
Organised by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in China, the dialogues brought together more than 130 breeding experts, business leaders and intellectual property professionals from China, the Netherlands and other countries.
Participants examined policy, breeding technology, judicial protection, financial implications and commercial implementation, with variety rights emerging as a key consideration for breeders entering international markets, according to a press release.
Tsjeard Hoekstra, deputy ambassador at the Dutch embassy in China, emphasised that an internationally aligned variety rights system is a prerequisite for breeders to bring their best varieties to market.
Dutch experts outlined developments in their country’s variety rights protection and regulatory approach. Discussions also highlighted that responsibility for protecting varieties extends beyond breeders to businesses involved in sales and distribution.
Li Shenchong, director of the Flower Research Institute at the Yunnan Academy of Agricultural Sciences, called for greater respect for breeding innovation, standardised variety trading, stronger protection of breeding achievements and deeper cooperation. These priorities form part of China’s Initiative on Innovation and Protection of New Plant Varieties (Flowers).
For breeders navigating the lengthy process from initial selection to commercial launch, a stable protection system helps create the conditions needed to introduce new varieties.
A separate discussion explored the application of AI and robotics in floriculture, with Chinese and Dutch experts sharing practical experience with AI crop models.
Limited land availability has helped drive the Netherlands’ investment in efficient cultivation. Over decades, Dutch greenhouse technology has combined sensors, algorithms and growing expertise to reduce inputs and increase output. AI and robotic systems could accelerate that progress.
Erik Smidt, counsellor for agriculture, fisheries, food security and nature at the Dutch embassy in China, emphasised the importance of trusted partners when doing business in China.
He pointed to more than two decades of cooperation between Dutch and Chinese floriculture businesses as a foundation for combining cultivation expertise with emerging technologies.
Across both discussions, participants identified cooperation as essential to advancing the flower sector, through stronger protection for breeding innovations and technologies that help growers produce more efficiently.

articles.title_orig: Musk has little to show for his record spending on Republican campaigns in US midterms
articles.title_zh: Musk has little to show for his record spending on Republican campaigns in US midterms
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk poured nearly half a billion dollars into the midterms to support Republican candidates, most to help Ken Paxton defeat Democrat James Talarico in the Texas Senate race.
Talarico won. But it was the other Democrat upsets in the state, for governor and attorney general, that could cause bigger problems for Musk and his Texas-based companies: rocket and AI company SpaceX and electric car maker Tesla.
Not only will he likely face greater regulatory scrutiny, but both candidates took direct aim at Musk and his businesses while on the campaign trail.
“It’s less about the blue wave on the Senate or House side,” said tech analyst Daniel Ives, a SpaceX and Tesla bull, about what Tuesday’s election results mean for Musk. “It’s more with the Texas governor.”
Democrat Nathan Johnson, who is replacing Paxton as Texas attorney general, said in July that, if elected, he would investigate whether SpaceX’s Starlink service was unfairly awarded grants designed to expand rural broadband. The internet service is SpaceX’s most profitable unit.
And Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, who unseated incumbent Greg Abbott, made opposition to data centers a major plank of her campaign. She has vowed to put a moratorium on new data center construction. Both Tesla and SpaceX have banked their future success on their AI efforts.
The biggest winners and losers of the 2026 midterm elections
SpaceX is planning major investments in new data centers in the next year, including the massive Colossal 3 to be built just outside of Brownsville, Texas. Unlike a lot of artificial intelligence companies, SpaceX earns a profit from selling time on its servers and cloud platforms to other AI companies. Hinojosa’s proposed moratorium would be a critical blow to its plans.
“I mean, those Texas data center plans are a key part of Musk’s ambitions,” Ives said. He said that’s why SpaceX and Tesla shares fell Wednesday, both dropping more than 3%, even as many other tech stocks rose.
Musk, the world’s richest person with a net worth estimated at about $898 billion, likely won’t sweat the money he lost backing Republicans, or even Wednesday’s decline in value for his shares.
How AI companies spent money on the midterms
The bigger issue for Musk is an increased level of scrutiny, which he noted on his social media platform, X, on Wednesday.
“Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Musk wrote, referencing his ultimate ambitions.
Experts say lifting and operating data centers in outer space still face many hurdles. But even if it was possible, SpaceX may have to take off from a spaceport in Louisiana if Texas moves to limit launches.
SpaceX has faced public criticism for the operation of its spaceport, “Starbase,” on Texas’ Gulf Coast. Some residents near the launch facilities have long expressed worries about disruptive sonic booms — which can be as loud as gunshots and register as small earthquakes — and collectively filed a lawsuit this year.
Musk bankrolling group using AI to attack Talarico on AI
SpaceX did not respond to a request for comment about the lawsuit. But Musk has previously downplayed sonic booms, saying in a 2022 post on X that “storms and hurricanes that are far more serious than Starship launches.”
Those resident complaints, however, could find a more sympathetic ear from Hinojosa compared to Abbott. (Hinojosa’s campaign did not respond to questions from CNN about her position on the spaceport.)
Tesla also has a big operation in Texas, and its driverless “robotaxis” only operate in four cities in Texas and three cities in Florida. For comparison, rival Waymo, a unit of Alphabet, operates in 15 cities across the country.
Local governments decide which vehicles, self-driving or otherwise, are allowed on their roads.
“It would it would be a big blow if robotaxis faced more regulation,” Ives said.
Tesla hasn’t listed profits or losses for its robotaxi service. But Musk has made it clear that Tesla’s future is selling rides in its robotaxis, not car sales. And a large part of Tesla’s evaluation is the expectation that its robotaxi service will eventually operate nationwide, Ives said.
Ives also says Hinojosa’s threat to the AI industry goes beyond just SpaceX. Texas is a key to US AI development. The state has the most planned data centers in the country, according to research firm Cleanview, and is second only to Virginia for the number open or under construction.
“Hinojosa is a known anti-data center politician and negative on the AI buildout which makes worries around the future of the datacenter buildout in Texas a real issue for tech investors,” Ives said in a note to investors Wednesday. “SpaceX stock will be under pressure.”

articles.title_orig: AI Stocks Crater as Citi Research Flags New Data Center Risk - Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD), Micro
articles.title_zh: AI Stocks Crater as Citi Research Flags New Data Center Risk - Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD), Micro
articles.content_orig:
The stock market tanked on Thursday amid concerns that a shift in congressional political control following the U.S. midterm elections could slow the construction of data centers that power artificial intelligence services.
Stocks sank across the board, but technology companies with a hand in the AI sector were hit especially hard. The Nasdaq Composite Index tumbled 1,422 points, or 5.5%, to close at 24,315. The drop means the tech-heavy index is now in a "correction," or down more than 10% from its most recent all-time high, set in October.
The broader S&P 500 dropped 335 points, or 4.4%, to end at 7,354, while the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 1,833 points, or 3.4%.
Market watchers think the Democrats' sweeping electoral victories this week could bolster opponents of data centers and slow the rollout of the facilities, which have spurred widespread public opposition. Investors are reacting to the growing "headline" risks around AI, according to Wall Street analyst Adam Crisafulli of Vital Knowledge.
The rout was violent enough to potentially delay the highly anticipated initial public offering by Anthropic , a bellwether for the entire AI business, Crisafulli told investors in a research note. Before the turmoil in financial markets, the IPO had been expected to take place this month and to raise as much as $100 billion.
The sharp drop also marks a sharp reversal from Wednesday, when the Dow posted its biggest gain of the year. Other indexes also surged after the election results eased uncertainty about who will control Washington.
"Even though the market rallied Wednesday after the midterm elections, there were visible cracks in the AI ecosystem, and they widened on Thursday amid investor concerns about a potentially slower data center buildout with Democrats in charge of Congress," Chris Larkin, a managing director of trading and investing for E*TRADE from Morgan Stanley, said in an email.
A slowdown in erecting data centers could deal a major blow to AI companies, which are pouring billions into the buildout and banking on widespread adoption of the technology.
"The trigger for these moves appears to be the concern that the Democrats, both in Congress and at the state level, will seek to regulate the AI industry and restrict data center development," Joe Maher, markets economist with investment adviser Capital Economics, said in a report. "The immediate risk is that restrictions on data center construction slow the pace of the AI infrastructure buildout. That is an obvious headwind for the firms directly involved in that buildout, whose prospects depend on continued rapid capex growth.
Investors worry that the enormous investment in AI is creating a stock market bubble, which happens when sky-high valuations become detached from companies' underlying fundamentals.
"Whether the midterms shock turns out to be the catalyst that derails the AI equity boom remains to be seen, but it strengthens our sense that the boom is in its final innings," Maher said.
Chip and other AI-exposed stocks took a particular beating on Thursday. Shares of Nvidia, whose advanced chips are a key component in developing ever more powerful AI models, fell 9.2% a day after dropping 3.2%. Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 17.3%. CoreWeave, a company that rents access to AI chips to customers over the cloud, fell 9.8%.
Trump Media & Technology Group, which owns the Truth Social platform, also continued to flail, with its shares falling 10.5% after dropping nearly 25% on Wednesday. The stock, which now hovers around $4, is at an all-time low since the company publicly listed its shares in March of 2024.
In other financial markets, the initial reaction to the election results faded a bit. The price of a barrel of Brent crude oil rose 2.6% to $97.11 and recovered much of its nearly 9% drop from the day before. Uncertainty still reigns about what will happen in the war with Iran and when the global energy industry can return to normal.

articles.title_zh: Bomb threats hit multiple flights in Europe for a second time in a week
articles.content_orig:

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Bomb threats across Europe have grounded flights across several countries and caused travel disruptions on Thursday.
It marks the second time this week that such widespread threats have been reported prompting fear and concern against the backdrop of a series of cyber-attacks affecting supermarket fridges and blood banks across the continent.
Flights flying to and from the UK , Belgium , Ireland, Italy , Finland , Bulgaria , Spain and Denmark were impacted and were largely resolved by the end of the day.
More than a dozen flights were targeted, included those from Copenhagen , Dublin , Helsinki , Madrid, Milan and Warsaw.
A Finnair plane from Helsinki was safely escorted to its scheduled landing in Rome by Italian Air Force jets. A Ryanair aircraft landed at Sofia airport after planes flying from Copenhagen and Madrid landed in the Bulgarian capital, according to the country’s interior minister.
Inspections of three Ryanair aircraft that received bomb threats and landed at the Bulgarian airports did not identify any issues, the country’s transport ministry said.
“Upon landing, the necessary inspections were carried out in accordance with the applicable procedures and no issues were identified,” the country’s transport ministry told Reuters. Airport operations at both Sofia and Plovdiv airports have returned to normal, it said.
Airports in the UK were also impacted amid threats reported at Heathrow and Birmingham airports.
“Threats reported at Heathrow and Birmingham in the early hours of this morning have been resolved,” a government spokesperson said in a statement issued on Thursday.
“It’s right that authorities treat any potential threats seriously — the UK has one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any threats, as well as malicious hoaxes, like those we’ve seen this week.”
The Times reported that the Metropolitan Police are continuing to monitor the situation.
Finnair also said that its two affected flights had landed safely after being affected by bomb threats.
Flights AY1761 from Helsinki to Rome and AY1471 from Helsinki to Vienna, faced unfounded or hoax bomb threats, the company said.
“Both flights landed safely at their destinations, and customers have disembarked the aircraft,” it said and added that nothing suspicious was found on the planes.
The plane to Rome was inspected and will depart back to Helsinki, while the flight to Vienna will “return to traffic normally after inspection.”
The incidents followed hoax bomb threats earlier this week that prompted searches, diversions and, in one case, a military escort across at least seven flights in Europe. An airport in Poland was forced to close in a day of chaos on Tuesday.
“Malicious” bomb scares on two flights from London , and others from Manchester, Copenhagen, Israel , Dublin, Bergamo and Lisbon threw airports into disarray, with authorities searching planes after some of the flights were forced to undergo emergency landings.
Hundreds of passengers on board were affected as well as others who had been affected by the temporary closures of airports.
On Wednesday, the French health ministry said that blood banks in France had been hit by a cyberattack amid a series of online hoaxes and cyberattacks.
“Several regional facilities of the French Blood Establishment (EFS) were affected by a cybersecurity incident that impacted certain cold storage room monitoring and control systems,” the ministry said.
Meanwhile, stores in eight European countries were forced to throw away vast quantities of food after hackers tampered with their fridges on Monday, mirroring hacks that swept dozens of supermarkets in France three weeks ago.

“ABB and SoftBank are in close dialogue and are working constructively on the transaction,” the Zurich-based automation giant wrote in a statement issued this morning.
The Financial Times, which first reported the news , notes that China represents Softbank Robotics’ largest market, employing more than 12,700 in the region. It adds that the country’s regulatory bodies were largely expected to approve the deal, which was announced last October.

articles.title_zh: Communist Party of Vietnam delegation pays working visit to China
articles.content_orig:
A delegation of the Communist Party of Vietnam (CPV) led by Nguyen Thanh Nghi, member of the Political Bureau, Secretary of the CPV Central Committee, and head of the committee’s Commission for Policy and Strategy, paid a working visit to China from November 1 to 5. The visit followed the fifth plenary session of the 20th central committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC).
Nghi met with Wang Huning, member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC); held talks with He Lifeng, member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, Vice Premier, and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Financial and Economic Affairs; and had a working session with Lu Hao, member of the CPC Central Committee and Director of the Development Research Centre of the State Council of China.
He congratulated China on its tremendous and comprehensive development achievements and the success of the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, held from October 26–29, describing it as an important theoretical preparation for the CPC’s 21st National Congress. He further expressed confidence that China would successfully implement the Resolution of the 20th National Congress of the CPC, successfully convene the 21st National Congress, and achieve its goal of building China into a modern socialist country that is prosperous, strong, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful.
Nghi also briefed the Chinese side on the implementation of the resolution of Vietnam’s 14th National Party Congress and the country’s socio-economic development, as well as several key policies and orientations adopted at the fourth plenum of the Party Central Committee.
Highlighting the long-standing friendship between Vietnam and China and Vietnam’s policy of giving top priority to developing ties with China, he affirmed that the Vietnamese Party and State stand ready to work with their Chinese counterparts to further strengthen political trust, enhance strategic connectivity, elevate substantive cooperation and support each other in their respective development processes.
Appreciating the significance of the visit, which followed a series of exchanges and meetings between the two countries’ high-ranking leaders, the Chinese leaders affirmed that China always regards relations with Vietnam as a priority in its neighbourhood diplomacy and supports Vietnam in playing a greater international role.
The two sides spoke highly of the positive and comprehensive progress in Vietnam-China relations and agreed to strengthen the leadership and guidance of the two Parties over ministries, sectors, agencies and localities in both countries.
China welcomed Vietnam’s participation in its ‘Big Market for All: Export to China’ initiative. It also expressed readiness to further increase imports of Vietnamese agricultural products and support capable Chinese enterprises in expanding investment in Vietnam.
Following the talks in Beijing the delegation visited Hangzhou, the capital of Zhejiang province.

articles.title_orig: Oman Sultan, Iran and Saudi envoys visit China
articles.title_zh: Oman Sultan, Iran and Saudi envoys visit China
articles.content_orig:
At the invitation of President Xi Jinping, Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman paid a state visit to China from November 1 to 2. This was the first China visit by an Omani head of state since diplomatic ties were established 48 years ago in 1978.
Ding Long, a professor at the Middle East Studies Institute of Shanghai International Studies University, told Global Times that with tensions mounting in the Strait of Hormuz, and Oman, which has been a long-standing active mediator in regional disputes, coming under pressure as well, the visit reflects the country’s efforts to strengthen strategic support and enhance diplomatic autonomy.
Oman is the only member of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) to consistently maintain positive relations with Iran, and it has played a pivotal role in regional diplomacy, including hosting rounds of talks between Iran and the United States. Its peaceful policy has earned at least one threat from US President Donald Trump to bomb the country.
Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said on November 2. He said that China stands ready to work with Oman to steer their strategic partnership to a higher level, and to help restore peace and realise lasting stability in the Middle East at an early date. China and Oman, he added, should enhance political mutual trust and strengthen exchanges of experience in national governance, while expressing China’s support for Oman in safeguarding national independence, sovereignty, security and stability, and in independently exploring a development path suited to its national conditions. And China, he said, is ready to deepen the synergy of development strategies with Oman and to be a stable and reliable partner in the energy sector, a partner with promising potential in investment, and a partner in fostering innovation in advanced technologies.
“China has been actively committed to ending hostilities and promoting peace, aiming to contribute its wisdom and solutions to resolving the regional security predicament,” Xi said, adding that China will continue to advocate resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, and support regional countries in building a common home of good-neighbourliness, development, security and cooperation.
Stressing that China has been Oman’s largest trading partner for many years and Chinese enterprises’ investment in Oman has kept growing, Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said his country is ready to synergise development strategies with China and strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, industry, infrastructure, AI, science and technology, and other fields. He said Oman highly appreciates China’s just position on the Middle East issue and stands ready to maintain close coordination with China to uphold international law, advocate for the peaceful resolution of disputes, and jointly promote security and stability in the region and beyond.
Later that day, Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik met with Chinese Premier Li Qiang. Li said the talks between the two heads of state earlier that morning mapped out a new blueprint for further deepening the China-Oman strategic partnership. He expressed China’s willingness to strengthen the alignment of development strategies with Oman, deepen cooperation across the entire oil and gas industry chain, and carry out more high-quality clean energy projects and called on both sides to expand cooperation in areas such as agriculture and fisheries, aerospace satellites, information and communication, and artificial intelligence, and promote the early conclusion of the free trade agreement negotiations between China and the GCC. He stressed that China and Oman, both Global South countries, should maintain close communication and coordination in multilateral affairs to jointly safeguard world peace and stability.
Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said Oman deeply admires China’s development achievements, which have attracted attention worldwide. Oman looks forward to learning from China’s development experience and deepening mutually beneficial cooperation between the two countries. Oman is willing to enhance communication and coordination with China in international and regional affairs and to contribute to resolving conflicts and maintaining peace and stability in the Middle East and the Gulf region.
In a potentially significant but under-reported related development, also on November 2, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met separately with the Deputy Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council and the National Security Advisor of Saudi Arabia.
Meeting with Deputy Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Ali Bagheri Kani, Wang Yi stated that China-Iran relations have maintained steady development despite a volatile international landscape. This serves the fundamental interests of both peoples and reflects the aspirations of Global South countries for solidarity and cooperation. China supports Iran in safeguarding its sovereignty and security and is willing to work with Iran to further advance bilateral relations.
Ali Bagheri Kani briefed Wang Yi on Iran’s views concerning the regional situation, stating that Iran would firmly safeguard its security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, and resist power politics and threats. Iran is also willing to engage in talks and negotiations with all parties and work actively for regional peace and stability. The Iranian side appreciates the initiatives and proposals put forward by President Xi Jinping and China’s consistent commitment to multilateralism. Iran looks forward to China playing a greater role in international and regional peace. Iran stands ready to promote the steady development of bilateral ties and to strengthen cooperation with China in international and multilateral frameworks.
In his meeting with Wang Yi, Saudi Arabia’s Minister of State, Member of the Council of Ministers, and National Security Advisor Musaad bin Mohammed Al-Aiban handed over a letter from Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman to President Xi Jinping regarding the development of China-Saudi bilateral relations and issues of mutual concern.
Wang Yi said that the current regional situation has once again reached a critical crossroads between war and peace. Although the road to peace is not smooth, it is necessary to keep moving forward. He hoped that all parties would resolve disputes and end the conflict through dialogue and negotiation, safeguarding regional energy and shipping security. China believes that countries in the region should enhance understanding, rebuild mutual trust, improve relations, and live harmoniously, promoting the construction of a new regional security framework that serves the long-term interests of their peoples through consultation.

articles.title_orig: Dow plunges 1,200 points, shedding most of midterm results stock rally - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Dow plunges 1,200 points, shedding most of midterm results stock rally - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
The selloff came a day after the Dow soared more than 1,500 points.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged about 1,200 points on Thursday, eroding most of the rally from a day earlier when midterm election results propelled the index to its best trading session in more than a year.
The S & P 500 dropped 3.2%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 4.8%, putting the index into correction territory, meaning it has fallen more than 10% from a previous peak last month.
The Dow declined 1,220 points, or 2.2%.
The selloff hammered many artificial intelligence firms as investors appeared to digest risk for the sector posed by newly empowered Democrats, many of whom ran campaigns critical of artificial intelligence data centers.
Nvidia, the chipmaking giant behind many of the semiconductors used in AI products, dropped 7% on Thursday. Rival chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices saw shares fall 12%. SanDisk, another AI hardware firm, plummeted more than 15% in value.
The slide also hit some other major tech firms behind AI development.
Microsoft, which holds a large stake in OpenAI, saw its stock price fall more than 2%. Amazon, which has spent hundreds of billions on its build-out of AI infrastructure, also dropped more than 2%.
The downturn in markets largely reversed blockbuster gains from the previous session.
On Wednesday, the Dow jumped 1,570 points, or 3%, recording its best one-day performance since April 9, 2025, when President Donald Trump announced the suspension of a far-reaching set of reciprocal tariffs.
Even as stocks climbed on Wednesday, Yorkville analyst Dan Ives warned ABC News of potential midterm fallout for the tech sector.
"The Democratic blue tidal wave across the Senate and House was a seismic shift that will have a negative impact on the pace of the AI Revolution buildout in the US over the next few years," Ives told ABC News in a statement.
Tuesday's midterm elections catapulted Democratic Senate and gubernatorial candidates to statewide victories in Republican strongholds like Ohio and Texas, both of which play host to a number of AI data centers.
A strong performance in House contests, meanwhile, appeared to set Democrats on a path toward a comfortable majority in the lower chamber.
OpenAI unveiled a new set of data center policies Thursday for that it called "responsible AI infrastructure" in the aftermath of the election.
The ChatGPT maker said it would abide by fresh commitments, including a vow to pay for all electricity and infrastructure used at its facilities. It also will create a "water plan" for each location as part of an effort to "protect local resources," and will "create opportunities for local workers and businesses" for employment, the AI company said in a blog post .

articles.title_orig: Nvidia has lost nearly $1.4 trillion since its October record
articles.title_zh: Nvidia has lost nearly $1.4 trillion since its October record
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Nvidia ( NVDA ) is on track for its fifth straight losing week, and the slide since its October record has now erased nearly $1.4 trillion in market value.
Thursday did a lot of the damage. At its morning low, Nvidia was down more than 9%, knocking nearly $450 billion off its market value in a matter of hours and leaving the company worth about $4.4 trillion. A close there would be the stock's worst day since the DeepSeek sell-off in January 2025.
Nvidia has plenty of company.
AMD ( AMD ), Micron ( MU ), and Arm ( ARM ) are posting steep double-digit losses, and Broadcom ( AVGO ) and Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) are falling near 10%. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) is now more than a third below its June record.
Nvidia itself is down nearly 25% from its Oct. 6 record close and trading below its 200-day moving average .
The trigger this time is Washington. Democrats won both chambers of Congress, and candidates in both parties campaigned against AI data centers , the buildings that run on Nvidia's chips. The Senate came close to passing a bill this fall that would have made data centers pay more of the power costs they create.
Losing streaks this long don't come often for Nvidia. Since its 1999 IPO, the stock has strung together five or more down weeks just 12 times before this one. The longest ran seven weeks, in the summer of 2008.
The last one is the streak bulls will want to remember. It ended in October 2022, about a month before ChatGPT's launch set off the AI boom, and Nvidia's stock roughly quadrupled over the following year.
That's the best case, not the base case. Nvidia was higher 13 weeks later in only five of the 12 earlier streaks, though it was up a year later in eight. The worst came in 2002, when the stock lost nearly two-thirds of its value over the following year.
For now, Washington is the new worry hanging over the stock.
"There will be congressional hearings," Stifel's Brian Gardner told Reuters ahead of the vote. "There will be investigations."

articles.title_orig: Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel’s next government
articles.title_zh: Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel’s next government
articles.content_orig:
The Joint List alliance of Arab-led parties says it will back Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government after last week’s election.
“The Joint List announced today, Thursday, that it will inform the President of the State, Isaac Herzog, this evening of its decision to recommend that Gadi Eisenkot be tasked with forming the government,” the alliance said in a statement.
Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats in Israel’s 120-seat parliament in last week’s general election, a result that could give them significant influence over the formation of the next government.
Once the Joint List’s 11 lawmakers formally submit their recommendation, Eisenkot is expected to have the backing of 67 lawmakers, exceeding the 61-seat majority threshold in the Knesset.
Earlier, Ra’am, an Arab-led party with eight seats, said it would also recommend Eisenkot.
Meanwhile, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc with 53 seats may not yield 53 endorsements, as Degel HaTorah, which holds four of United Torah Judaism’s seven seats, said it would recommend neither candidate.
The ultra-Orthodox faction broke with Netanyahu over his coalition’s failure to pass legislation exempting Haredi men from military service, The Times of Israel reported.
Netanyahu has also claimed repeatedly and without evidence that Arab parties committed fraud during the elections with foreign backing.
The prime minister and his Likud party have cited a handful of cases, including the arrests of three political activists who allegedly bribed voters before polls opened. They are suspected of connections with the Ra’am party, although the party denies any involvement.
Netanyahu and Likud also suggested that the opposition bloc joining with Arab-led parties would be treasonous. In a statement after the vote, Likud warned that Zionist parties cooperating with the Arab bloc would be “dangerous to Israel”.
Israel’s Central Elections Committee certified the results of the election on Wednesday after finding no evidence of fraud.
President Herzog has also accepted the results and begun consultations with party leaders on whom to task with forming the next government.
He also backed investigating suspected interference but warned against smearing voters who are Palestinian citizens of Israel, saying he had “great respect” for the country’s Palestinian minority, which makes up about 20 percent of the population.
“I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently,” he said.
On Wednesday, the president said he had met representatives of the Religious Zionism and Zehut, Shas and Yisrael Beytenu factions.
In a post on X, Herzog said he “received their recommendations regarding the identity of the Knesset member upon whom the task of forming the government should be assigned”.
Herzog added that talks would also continue on Thursday.
Once the consultations end, Herzog will choose the candidate he considers best placed to assemble a coalition, almost certainly Netanyahu or Eisenkot. He has several days to announce his decision, after which the nominee will have 28 days to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension.
If neither man succeeds, Israel would hold another election early next year.
Reporting from Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh said that if Eisenkot is able to form a government, then he will become Israel’s next prime minister and Netanyahu will likely be the head of the opposition.
“It is up to Gadi Eisenkot to do what he promised, to oust Benjamin Netanyahu. And to do that, he needs to have 61 votes in the Knesset, which means that he needs the votes of the Palestinian-Israeli parties, parties that he does not want to partner up with,” she said.
“But he will most likely have to reach some sort of deal, for [the Palestinian-Israeli parties] to abstain at the very least, to make sure that his government is sworn in and a new chapter in Israeli politics is able to begin,” she added.

articles.title_zh: After Riots and Protests, French Workers Are Going on Strike
articles.content_orig:
• General strike : French riot police have fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon while scuffles have broken out in Nantes and authorities have arrested agitators who vandalized a Rennes hotel. But overall, the roughly 200 demonstrations across France on Thursday – attended by almost 600,000 people – have remained relatively peaceful.
• Widespread disruptions : The strike is organized by L’intersyndicale, the group that represents all of France’s main trade unions. Education, health care, public transportation and other sectors have been impacted with many services closed for the day.
• Europe discontent : Anti-government protests have swept across the continent in recent weeks. In Greece , students and teachers gathered in central Athens on Thursday to stress the importance of free public education and protest the rising housing and food costs affecting students.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will hold a “social conference” with employers and unions next Monday as hundreds of thousands of people participate in protests across the country.
The conference will be aimed at addressing questions around “purchasing power and wages,” the prime minister’s office said in a statement .
Today’s general strike and protests have been organized by L’intersyndicale, the group that represents all of France’s main trade unions.
Place de la Nation, in eastern Paris, is a historic plaza synonymous with protest. Marches often end here, and we’re used to seeing huge clouds of tear gas as protesters clash with police.
But tonight, it’s quite an unusual and arresting sight to see the square so full after dark. A huge mass of people continue to stand still beneath a monument celebrating the triumph of the French Republic.
The protest in Paris was authorized by city officials to wrap up at 7 p.m. local time (1 p.m. ET). But with less than 30 minutes to go, it’s unlikely everyone will be able to disperse quickly.
Although this movement initially began with students protesting the state of the education system, it has morphed into one that includes several other concerns united by a key factor: the poor state of the economy.
Protesters on Thursday said they are anxious about low salaries, which have not kept up with inflation, as well as underresourced public services.
“There is a lot of concern about the future, notably the issues of salaries, public services,” Alice Martinovic, an 18-year-old student participating in the Paris protest, told Reuters.
“I hope in the upcoming elections the candidates will really think about this movement and include the opinions of young people, of students, who are now joined by a lot of other workers.”
Meanwhile, Mehdi Dumontroty, a 45-year-old firefighter also protesting in Paris, told Reuters that “our pay has not kept up with inflation.”
“What happened this summer proves that we were right when we said we needed more resources to deal with the crisis that we faced,” he said, referencing fierce wildfires which swept across southern France amid record-breaking, climate change-fueled heat waves.
Almost 600,000 protesters are on the streets of France today, the country’s interior ministry has just estimated, making Thursday the biggest day of protests since this current wave of unrest began in September.
Earlier today, at 1 p.m. local time (7 a.m. ET), the ministry had estimated that 270,000 people were protesting but that number excluded Paris, where a march began this afternoon.
The ministry is expected to release its final figures later today but, as of now, its current estimates indicate that these demonstrations are not quite as big as the 2023 pension reform protests.
French education minister Édouard Geffray has condemned what he said was a “deliberate act of arson” at a school near the city of Toulouse in southern France.
The minister thanked firefighters and law enforcement officials for helping to “limit the damage” cause by the flames.
“This deliberate act of arson could have had tragic consequences for human life. I condemn it in the strongest possible terms and call on everyone to condemn it unequivocally,” he added, while vowing to hold those responsible to account.
Earlier, France’s interior ministry said the blaze started after fireworks were directed at an office hosting the school’s student services.
Authorities in Rennes said they arrested “several dozen” masked individuals who vandalized a hotel, threw objects at police and “violently attacked” union members who were protesting earlier today.
Photos taken by local media show that vandals smashed the hotel’s glass doors and painted graffiti on windows.
Some masked individuals also tried to erect barricades to block some of the city’s roads, lit fires in garbage bins, and threw heavy pétanque balls – used in a popular French game – at police, authorities added.
Despite violent clashes like this, however, the protests today have largely been peaceful even as they have been attended by hundreds of thousands of people.
As today’s march in Paris got underway, the trade unions were in a jubilant mood. Music blared out as the crowd, dominated by left-wing groups, sang and chanted slogans against the government and the far-right.
A police helicopter buzzed above, but in the confines of the avenue we were walking down, there was little sense of the heavy police presence around the protest.
In the distance, the soaring statue of Marianne – the national symbol of France – got smaller and smaller as the march inched its way forward.
The protest route is packed. The movement of the crowd has been brought to a near standstill at points by the sheer quantity of people.
Later, several protesters were seen lying on the ground being treated by street medics, with blood flowing from the head of an older man. A bystander said the man was struck by police, but an officer at the scene said they were unaware of any incident.
At one point, protesters scattered as tear gas was deployed by police, followed by mass cries of “everyone hates the police.”
The mood of the crowd has lost its upbeat feel.
Several of France’s biggest unions, representing everyone from students, teachers and postal workers to doctors, pharmacists and transport workers, have called for a nationwide strike. So, how is that affecting these essential services?
Schools: About 13% of all school staff are participating in the strikes, France’s education ministry estimates, including 16% of all teachers. Around 19% of schools and 18% of colleges across France are affected by the strike.
Universities: About one in three of France’s higher education are “disrupted” because of the strikes and protests, the government told CNN.
Hospitals: Very few public hospital staff – only about 4% of the workforce – are participating in the strike, France’s healthcare ministry told CNN. “No significant disruption to healthcare services has been reported,” the ministry added. Two of France’s main unions representing both public and private healthcare workers had called on them to strike, citing the high cost of living and the deterioriation of public services.
Transport: Four in 10 of today’s scheduled trains have been canceled, though a handful of those cancelations are due to other factors like unavailable equipment, according to tracking website Trayn.
The labor unions that have called today’s demonstrations in France are demanding higher wages and pensions. In particular, the largest of the unions – the CGT – says the minimum wage needs to be increased immediately by 10%.
Last month, the CGT claimed there had been a big increase in the number of professions paying some employees less than the minimum wage. Another union - the CFDT – is demanding a 100 euro increase in the minimum monthly wage, about 7%.
Maud Millier, a CGT official in Lyon, said that the government’s announced minimum wage increase, from November 1, amounts to just €15 for someone earning the minimum wage, which she said was nowhere near enough given rising fuel and food pr

articles.title_orig: Putin seizes Russian operations of Japanese tobacco giant JTI
articles.title_zh: Putin seizes Russian operations of Japanese tobacco giant JTI
articles.content_orig:
Illustrative photo. Source: Alexander Roumega / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.
JSC Industrial Assets took over JTI’s production facilities in Rostov-on-Don, Yelets and St. Petersburg. The decree does not specify which of the several Russian companies with that name received the assets.
Russian President Vladimir Putin placed the assets of tobacco products maker JTI Donskoy Tabak in Rostov-on-Don under external administration, Radio Liberty’s Kavkaz.Realii project reports. The company belonged to Japanese holding company JTI, one of the world’s largest tobacco producers.
This is reported by Radio Svoboda .
The decree says that production facilities in Rostov-on-Don, Yelets and St. Petersburg were transferred to JSC Industrial Assets. Several joint-stock companies with that name are registered in Russia, and the document does not specify which one received the assets.
The Russian outlet Agentstvo found that one of these companies was established just a few weeks ago. Its owner is Sergey Dremov, a former FSB employee linked to state corporation Rostec. Other companies called Industrial Assets are run, among others, by Teymuraz Bolloev, who took over the Baltika brewing company after the war began, and by Armen Sarkisyan, the owner of Stoloto, the outlet Important Stories reports.
In 2018, former owner of Donskoy Tabak, Rostov-born Greek entrepreneur Ivan Savvidi, sold the company to Japanese investors for 1.6 billion rubles. After the invasion of Ukraine began, JTI remained in Russia but halted investment. Ukraine’s National Agency on Corruption Prevention added the company to its list of international sponsors of war.
JTI Donskoy Tabak makes cigarettes and tobacco products under the Winston, Camel, LD, Sobranie and Mevius brands, as well as Ploom tobacco-heating systems.
In September, Putin placed the main Russian entities of retailers Auchan and Leman PRO, logistics company FM Logistic and food producer Nestle under temporary management. JSC L.E.V. Management was appointed as the managing company. The Kremlin spokesperson explained that the owners of these companies came from European countries that Moscow considers “unfriendly.”

articles.title_orig: China Resources Longdation's Aethereal Cybersecurity and GCSA Jointly Establish the Centre for AI and Cybersecurity Research
articles.title_zh: China Resources Longdation's Aethereal Cybersecurity and GCSA Jointly Establish the Centre for AI and Cybersecurity Research
articles.content_orig:
HONG KONG , Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- China Resources Longdation's Aethereal Cybersecurity and Global Cybersecurity Alliance Limited (GCSA) have announced the joint establishment of the Centre for AI and Cybersecurity Research. The initiative brings together both parties' technological expertise and industry resources in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and industrial applications to advance research, product innovation, and industry collaboration.
Founded in 1982, China Resources Longdation operates across property management, asset management, and community services. Its Aethereal Cybersecurity business specializes in AI-driven digital transformation and cybersecurity services for government agencies and enterprises, providing professional technologies and solutions to Hong Kong SAR 's government departments, public institutions, and businesses, supported by relevant cybersecurity qualifications. GCSA is committed to advancing technological innovation, research collaboration, and international exchange in cybersecurity, with a particular focus on emerging security challenges involving AI, Web3, and digital finance.
The two parties will strengthen their cooperation in cybersecurity. The Centre will focus on joint research and development in AI-powered fraud prevention, cyber threat detection, digital financial security, and cybersecurity automation. Key areas of exploration include AI deception honeypots, intelligent fraud detection, threat intelligence analysis, and security platforms, with an emphasis on practical applications.
By combining their respective resources and professional service capabilities, the partnership aims to foster cross-organizational collaboration in AI and cybersecurity, contributing to the development of the digital economy and cybersecurity industry.
Contact: Laber Mann, media@gcsa.com

articles.title_orig: Clashes erupt in France as ‘Black Thursday’ protests sweep the nation
articles.title_zh: Clashes erupt in France as ‘Black Thursday’ protests sweep the nation
articles.content_orig:
PARIS — Riot police clashed with protesters in Lyon on Thursday as a nationwide public sector strike tapped into growing anger over deteriorating services and the rising cost of living.
Paris’ iconic Eiffel Tower was closed because of the strike.
Officers clad in black helmets and protective clothing charged at crowds in Lyon after the demonstrations against rising living costs and in support of the high school protest movement turned violent and fires were set in the streets. Water cannons were also deployed. Some of the protesters wore gas masks and safety glasses as a precaution against tear gas.
Images from Paris showed students and other protesters facing off against riot police.
Police were “keeping the situation under control, but it remains tense,” the French Interior Ministry said in a statement at 1 p.m. local time (7 a.m. ET).
“Several violent acts have been committed as part of the high school student movement,” the statement said. After fireworks were fired at a school near the southern city of Toulouse, a fire broke out “that burned the student services office,” it added.
In the city of Rennes in northwest France, metal pétanque balls were thrown at officers, the statement said, adding that police had been pelted with other projectiles in the cities of Pau and Orleans.
Around 250 rallies against rising living costs had been planned in cities and towns across the country and hundreds of thousands of people would likely turn out, unions said before the events kicked off.
France’s main unions, including the CGT and CNT representing public and private sector workers, and the UNEF, representing students, warned the government of President Emmanuel Macron’s that the country was on the brink or recession.
“Everything is going up except wages and pensions,” they said in a joint statement. “Anger is immense.”
“The situation in this country is fragile. The pressing social and environmental challenges must be addressed without delay,” the statement added.
The movement grew from a student protest over staff shortages at the Antoine de Saint-Exupéry High School in Créteil, a southeastern suburb of Paris. Videos of the blockade spread on social media, and soon protests expanded to high schools across the nation.
As the movement grew, the list of grievances expanded beyond the failings of the public school system to encompass broader economic, political and social dissatisfaction. Soon, university students, teachers, parents and politicians also joined.
Hundreds of thousands of protesters have since taken to the streets as the demonstrations expanded, with participants holding signs criticizing the far-right National Rally party and warning of the risks of climate change and artificial intelligence. A multitude of Palestinian flags have also been seen.
Macron, who will leave office in May, convened a defense ‌and security meeting Wednesday ahead of the protests. Later, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that 70,000 police officers would be deployed Thursday, backed by armored vehicles, drones and helicopters.
Police have previously been criticized for injuring protesters with heavy-handed tactics. Last month, a 15-year-old was maimed by a sting ball grenade fired by police and a 14-year-old suffered a jaw fracture in a similar incident.
Several other have also suffered life-changing injuries and a 59-year-old man, identified as Christophe M, died Oct. 17 of “a critical cardio-respiratory failing” after leaving Paris’ Place de la République which had been tear-gassed be police. An investigation into his death is ongoing.
Zacharie Petit reported from Paris and Henry Austin from London.
Zacharie Petit is a producer in Paris.
Henry Austin is a senior editor for NBC News Digital based in London.

articles.title_orig: Bad News for Italian Chef Who Balked at Pineapple Pizza
articles.title_zh: Bad News for Italian Chef Who Balked at Pineapple Pizza
articles.content_orig:
An Italian chef sacked from a Brisbane restaurant had refused to put pineapple on a pizza because it was an "insult to his culture".
Davide Tamburella was fired from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in May, a fortnight after a meeting with management who had a string of complaints about the chef's behaviour.
Among them were Tamburella's refusal to provide ham and pineapple pizza for guests at a function. At the time, the chef had stated that any direction from management "need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture".
The details came to light after the chef went to Australia's Fair Work Commission claiming he had been unfairly dismissed.
In its ruling released on Tuesday, the commission noted that Tamburella's refusal to put pineapple on the pizzas was because "he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture".
It also noted that it was the third time Tamburella had refused to use the fruit on pizzas in the past four years.
He had previously requested his boss to "check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza".
The state of Queensland, where the restaurant is located, is considered Australia's pineapple heartland and produces all of the country's commercially-grown pineapples.
On the Sunshine Coast, visitors regularly stop to take photos next to The Big Pineapple, a heritage-listed 16m-tall fibreglass model of the fruit, which has become a local landmark.
Other concerns were raised about Tamburella using foul language, his communication style and "escalation of frustration in the workplace".
The ruling also detailed an incident at work in April this year where Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand when he struck a metal hand rail.
Tamburella had been hoping the restaurant would sponsor a visa for him that allows skilled workers to be permanent residents.
However after his sacking, the restaurant ended that  process, the tribunal heard.
He lost his unfair dismissal claim on the grounds that the application had been filed too late, according to the ruling.
The restaurant's managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was "more to this story than a pizza topping".
The BBC has approached Tamburella for comment.
On the chef's LinkedIn profile, he describes himself as someone who, throughout his career, has focused on "delivering exceptional food" and "improving business performance".
Three months ago he posted a "letter for chefs" with the theme "respecting the ingredients".
The LinkedIn profile states he now works at another Brisbane restaurant. A BBC check has found that pineapple is not on its menu.

articles.title_orig: Record share of first-time homebuyers paying in cash as Great Wealth Transfer picks up steam
articles.title_zh: Record share of first-time homebuyers paying in cash as Great Wealth Transfer picks up steam
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
The Great Wealth Transfer is starting to impact the housing market.
A record share of first-time homebuyers are paying for their properties in cash, a sign that more buyers are likely using money they inherited from older generations to help fund their purchases.
Last year, 1 in 10 first-time buyers did an all-cash transaction, according to a new report from the National Association of Realtors, the fourth straight year with an increase, and the largest share since the trade group began collecting data on those transactions in 2003. Among first-time all-cash buyers, 28% reported using an inheritance to help fund their deal, compared with just 9% of first-time buyers who financed.
As home prices hover near all-time highs and mortgage rates stay north of 7% , pricing out many prospective buyers, some portion of those buyers may simply be waiting for an inheritance or other significant help from wealthy baby boomers or members of the Silent Generation.
"It is critical when analyzing first-time buyers to understand there is a growing divide among those who are saving independently and priced out of homeownership, versus those who are waiting on the sidelines but then given a generational transfer of wealth," the report said.
Buyers reliant on wealth transfers look different from those who finance and use their own savings. As modern life expectancy increases, delaying inheritances, first-time all-cash buyers are typically deep into middle age. The median first-time buyer paying all cash is 54 years old, according to the report, significantly older than the median age of 38 for first-time buyers financing their homes.
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title_orig: AI backlash threatens trillion-dollar data centre boom, say tech leaders
articles.title_zh: AI backlash threatens trillion-dollar data centre boom, say tech leaders
articles.content_orig:
A stunning upset in the Texas governor race and sweeping Democratic victories across the country threaten to curtail the biggest-ever spending boom in US history.
That could disrupt a key growth engine for America’s economy .
Come January, states controlled by Democrats who support expanding or extending AI construction moratoriums will account for 45% of America’s planned data center capacity, according to Goldman Sachs. A quarter of America’s planned AI infrastructure buildout is set to take place in Texas alone.
That doesn’t mean half of America’s planned data centers are on hold. Demand for AI is off the charts. Donald Trump is still president, and he’s already waving around his veto hat. And Democratic governors couldn’t stop every data center from being constructed even if they wanted to.
But Tuesday’s election nevertheless represents a paradigm shift that could alter the pace and path of America’s nonstop AI spending spree – an investment boom that has, according to ING economists, accounted for as much as a quarter of total US economic growth this year.
Communities fighting against the buildings that power AI
Those economic benefits are already real, supporting thousands of jobs. And AI has the potential to revolutionize the way we work.
But an AI data center slowdown could come with important silver linings. It could rein in unfettered growth that has contributed to rebounding inflation and led to widespread public antipathy toward the technology and the data centers that house it. It could also curtail some questionable business models that have raised serious skepticism on Wall Street.
Tapping the brakes could ultimately put AI – and the US economy – on a more sustainable path.
AI infrastructure spending is expected to approach $1 trillion a year, every year, for the foreseeable future, according to Columbia Business School economist Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh. As a percentage of America’s gross domestic product, that would outpace every other investment boom in modern US history – including the construction of the railroads.
The outcome of Tuesday’s elections could slow that spending, with vast consequences for the thousands of jobs and massive amounts of economic development that AI supports.
Democrats gained gubernatorial seats in Nevada, Georgia, Ohio and Texas, where candidates campaigned on tightening data center regulations. Proposals from the governors-elect include ending tax breaks, tightening climate and electricity restrictions and allowing local governments to impose their own moratoriums on data center construction.
But Texas is the big kahuna. Wells Fargo estimates that for every 10% reduction in planned Texas data center capacity, Big Tech companies will reduce their AI infrastructure spending by a stunning 1.6% (a lot of money when you’re measuring spending in the trillions of dollars).
State and local politicians have a lot of jurisdiction and sway over that spending: enough to change whether some projects get financed, said Mona Dajani, co-chair of Cooley’s infrastructure, energy and real estate practice.
Hundreds of data center developments that are still awaiting permits, utility service or tax incentives could be particularly exposed, Dajani noted. But even active construction projects could be threatened. Texas law grandfathers in some projects’ permits, protecting them from future changes to local permitting requirements – but that doesn’t resolve state permitting changes or electrical service guarantees that Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa could vacate.
The wait for approvals could add significant costs for AI companies, Dajani said: Interest, equipment commitments and utility expenses will all continue to accrue, even while a project is on ice. At some point, existing projects could stop being financially viable.
If that happens, AI companies – who have already strained to build out data centers fast enough to meet their anticipated demand – may not be able to meet their explosive spending targets.
“This is a rare case where state and local leaders have influence of geopolitical-level import,” said Harry Krejsa, director of studies at the Carnegie Mellon Institute for Strategy & Technology.
Data centers aren’t exclusively a Democratic issue: Americans have displayed bipartisan consensus for putting guardrails around data center buildouts.
Texas Republican Governor Greg Abbott had already imposed a data center moratorium that Hinojosa campaigned on extending until lawmakers establish stronger AI regulations.
But Trump had railed against any attempts to stymie AI’s growth and spending, citing economic and national security – particularly in the high-stakes race against China. Many Republican politicians who may have otherwise supported AI regulations, including frameworks for data center construction, remained silent.
Still, there’s evidence that the AI buildout could be on an unsustainable path.
The United States had 5,427 data centers at the end of last year, according to Stanford University’s AI Index Report , and AI companies have announced plans for 3,969 new US data centers, according to Aterio , a data center research company. But only about 800 are under construction, and AI experts have raised doubts about the viability of many of the announced projects.
If Tuesday’s election results trigger an investment slowdown, that could trim some of the industry’s fat.
Example A: CoreWeave, a neocloud business that rents out computing capacity, recently projected such extensive losses that its bond yields surged to 15% – the danger zone. That was particularly troubling, because its expected return on investment was only around 9%.
In other words, CoreWeave loses money on every single dollar it spends on expanding its data center capacity.
Deep-pocketed hyperscalers – Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft – don’t have that problem. But their stocks have been slammed in recent weeks as investors grow impatient with what they view as an unsustainable amount of spending that may not return profits for years.
“AI is catching a break here,” said Joe Brusuelas, chief economist at RSM US.
Brusuelas expects growth to slow from last quarter’s 3.4% pace to something closer to 2.4% if there is an AI slowdown. That’s still solid long-term growth. And America’s economy is massive and diverse. Investment that otherwise would have gone to data centers can go elsewhere.
“It’s slowing, but it doesn’t mean we’re going to have a recession,” Brusuelas said.
It also presents an opportunity for AI companies to get smart about their future AI data center rollouts – and get put on a more sustainable course.
The helter-skelter approach to data center construction has resulted in significant amounts of money getting flushed down the toilet in unworkable projects – collateral damage from massive competition to be first and biggest. Data centers already face $200 billion in project delays, according to Mike Mathews, global digital infrastructure practice leader at risk adviser Marsh.
A more rational, politically sensitive approach could create longer-term benefits for the communities that host the data centers and for the AI companies themselves.
There’s precedent for that. In the previous decade, the Googles of the world built out data centers for the cloud computing revolution, promoting the fact that they’d be built sustainably with renewable energy – even before it was cost-effective to do that. A similar, community-based approach could provide AI companies with the compute they need and give them the political and social license to operate their data centers for the long haul.
“Like the saying goes: If you want to go fast, you go it alone; if you want to go far you go together,” said Krejsa. “If you squander political license to operate at home, that’ll be a bigger impediment to remaining competitive with China.”

articles.title_orig: YouTube rolling out app redesign without Subscriptions tab, and everyone hates it
articles.title_zh: YouTube rolling out app redesign without Subscriptions tab, and everyone hates it
articles.content_orig:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.
Google seems to be taking multiple stabs at tweaking how the bottom navigation bar in the YouTube app looks and works. After removing the Subscriptions tab from the navigation bar , the company is now experimenting with a new floating design.
According to a Reddit post by user SameRecognition5543, Google has started testing a floating navigation bar in the YouTube app on Android. The design looks heavily inspired by the Liquid Glass aesthetic of iOS 27, leading some users to accuse Google of abandoning its own Material 3 Expressive design language in favor of Apple’s Liquid Glass.
Google seems to be running a very limited test for the floating navigation bar on Android. We checked on multiple devices and couldn’t spot the new navigation bar test on any of them. However, we did spot the new floating navigation bar on a couple of iPhones. Google may be prioritizing an iPhone rollout first, which makes sense since iOS introduced the Liquid Glass design language.
Meanwhile, if you like the new look and don’t want to wait for Google to eventually roll it out to your device, there is a workaround you can use. The Morphe YouTube patcher has already been updated with a similar floating navigation bar featuring a Liquid Glass design. First, enable pre-release patches in Morphe on your Android phone. Then, go to Settings > General > Navigation bar and turn on the “Enable glass navigation bar” toggle.
User opinion on the new floating navigation bar is split. Several users are waiting for the update to reach their devices and are using Morphe in the meantime. However, other users aren’t too happy about the iOS-like design. Either way, this might well be the future of YouTube’s navigation bar on Android. If you don’t like it, you can take solace in the fact that Google’s rollouts are infamously slow and phased, so you might not have to see it for a while, even when it does start rolling out.
Read what readers said or add your take.

You're exactly two weeks away from playing GTA 6 .
To celebrate the fact, developer Rockstar has shared another batch of screenshots that are designed to showcase Vice City at its best, and the world beyond. Take a look below at a whopping 37 new screenshots:
GTA 6 comes to PS5 on 19th November 2026, but you can get your preload started from 10th November. Learn more in our GTA 6 Release Times and Preload guide , which is staying up to date as we near launch.
A lot of the images focus on protagonists Jason and Lucia, but we do catch glimpses of other characters, the nightlife, and more that'll be part of Leonida. What's your favourite picture? Share it in the comments below.

@LifeGirl , you clearly have not played or seen GTA 5 next to GTA 6, or you need to visit an optician urgently.

I do have to say, I wonder whether it will live up to the hype, and also whether it will get fantastic 10/10 reviews whilst at the same time numerous issues with the game are pointed out? I wonder whether professional reviewers will feel compelled to give the game 10/10s, or whether it will deserve them, and whether those same issues in another game would see it marked down? In other words, is the game too big to be critiqued properly?

Laura Branigan, @GirlVersusGame ? Are you an old soul or just well versed on good music? I was there front of the queue to buy her first album when it released in 1982. I absolutely loved her...
All at a staggering beautiful 30fps. My time is on Zelda OOT.

@AI-Generation I'll be playing both
As I'm still waiting for a 60fps mode for RDR2 before buying it, I'll probably buy and play GTA6 on a second hand PS6 Pro.
@Fiendish-Beaver Music is a kind of obsession and Vice City, along with many other games in the series helped to introduce me to so many good bands and musicians. Music is a big part of why I want to experience Six. I tend to prefer older music, movies and people. You definitely experienced the better timeline.

@Boxmonkey I bet that if you took a random landscape screenshot from both games and put them side by side you would not be able to tell the difference.
Can’t wait. It’s all ready. Ps5 pro, LG G5 and my Soundsystem. My only concern are the 30 fps, especially on an OLED. We will see how this turns out. Even it’s absolutely unrealistic: still having a glimpse of hope for any kind of 40 fps mode.
Grand theft auto i6 is going to be a instant and win game of the year. Word up son
Only 2 more weeks! Also getting my new ( and slightly bigger 😁 ) Oled next tuesday, so im ready for GTA6.

As soon as im back on friday it will be on all weekend and not moving only for food drink and toilet 🤣. Im glad we havent had too many trailers for it, can go in relativley blind to it.

To me, it's a bit like everyone raving about the latest Artic Monkeys album, when I just don't like their music and I cannot understand how anyone does... 😉
Laura Branigan, @GirlVersusGame ? Are you an old soul or just well versed on good music? I was there front of the queue to buy her first album when it released in 1982. I absolutely loved her...
All at a staggering beautiful 30fps. My time is on Zelda OOT.
@Oram77 game has already done $750 million in sales and it's not out yet. It can't literally bomb. But it can be a massive let down enough to shake the entire gaming foundation. I don't think it will be. But I still hold reservation for performance issues plaguing this game from when CD showed 48 minutes of Cyberpunk "gameplay" and we all know how that turned out at launch.
@AI-Generation I'll be playing both
As I'm still waiting for a 60fps mode for RDR2 before buying it, I'll probably buy and play GTA6 on a second hand PS6 Pro.
